Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
1 October 2026 .
Brent $ 101.09 + 3.12 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Reuters reports three oil tankers were struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, with the attacker unidentified.

02 Brent crude stood at $101.09, up 3.12% over 24 hours, as of 14:56 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 Persian Gulf producers are shifting cargo transfer operations farther from the strait as waters outside Hormuz grow congested with tankers, per gCaptain.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the central operational pressure point for global energy flows. Reuters reports three oil tankers were struck by projectiles in the strait on Tuesday, with the attacker unidentified; gCaptain separately reports that Persian Gulf producers are pushing critical ship-to-ship transfer operations farther from the war-hit zone as waters just outside Hormuz grow congested. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent crude stood at $101.09, up 3.12% over 24 hours, as of 14:56 UTC. On the export side, CNBC reports that crude oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz have hit pre-war levels, though fuel shipments remain constrained; that figure measures barrels, not vessel crossings, and the two metrics continue to diverge. Indian refiners are adjusting logistics: Business Standard's headline says Indian oil refiners are changing tactics and hiring tankers to sail through Hormuz. On the diplomatic track, Iran said it received the US response to Foreign Minister Araghchi's seven-day plan and is reviewing it; the terms have not been published and no agreement has been reached. Iran's claim to have seized a US minehunting drone in the strait, relayed by Baird Maritime, has not been independently corroborated. The 32 indexed events in the past 24 hours keep the operational picture volatile. As of 14:50 UTC, 168 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
